newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia UES says paid atomic stations 129 bln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russia UES says paid atomic stations 129 bln rbls.

text.p: Russia's national power company UES said on Friday it had sent the country's beleaguered atomic energy stations 129 billion roubles ($22.2 million) to pay workers' wages and other expenses.

UES chief executive Boris Brevnov said the sum exceeded the 125.5 billion roubles ($21.6 million) agreed last month as a monthly payment after workers marched to Moscow to protest over six months of unpaid wages and other non-payments.
The march prompted President Boris Yeltsin to intervene and order officials to pay off the workers.
Workers in nuclear power stations and research facilities were at that point owed 250 billion roubles ($43 million at current rates), while consumers owed them hundreds of millions of dollars.
A UES spokesman said about one third of the money had come from the government.

Brevnov said the energy sector, at the centre of a nationwide payments crisis, currently owes the government about 5.4 trillion roubles ($861 million), while government debts to UES now stood at 18 trillion roubles ($3.1 billion).
Officials said a campaign to increase cash payments for power, including the start of a model wholesale power market, was starting to make progress.
